chapterFiles.title: Shi'ur Qomah — Siddur Rabbah recension: the cosmic measurements of the divine body and the magical names of its limbs

versionTitles.ja: ホイール・オブ・ヘブン訳

versionSource: Best-effort reconstruction from named scholarly editions (Jellinek 1853 Bet ha-Midrasch — PD; Cohen 1985 The Shi'ur Qomah: Texts and Recensions, TSAJ 9; Schäfer 1981 Synopse zur Hekhalot-Literatur)
sourceCitation: Cohen, Martin S., The Shi'ur Qomah: Texts and Recensions (Texte und Studien zum Antiken Judentum 9, Tübingen: Mohr Siebeck 1985) — THE modern critical edition. Cohen, Martin S., The Shi'ur Qomah: Liturgy and Theurgy in Pre-Kabbalistic Jewish Mysticism (Lanham: UPA 1983) — the companion study. Schäfer, Peter, Synopse zur Hekhalot-Literatur (Texte und Studien zum Antiken Judentum 2, Tübingen: Mohr Siebeck 1981) — the manuscript synopsis. Jellinek, Adolf, Bet ha-Midrasch: Sammlung kleiner Midraschim, vols. 2 & 6 (Leipzig 1853-1877; PD) — for the public-domain transmission. Scholem, Gershom, Major Trends in Jewish Mysticism (Jerusalem 1941; NY 1946) and Jewish Gnosticism, Merkabah Mysticism, and Talmudic Tradition (New York: JTS 1965) — foundational scholarship.

subtitles.en: The Hekhalot/Merkavah mystical text describing the cosmic dimensions of the divine body — Siddur Rabbah recension. The 'Kabbalah' the Raëlian canon implicitly cites for *parasangs* measurements.

descriptions.en: Shi'ur Qomah, the Jewish mystical text that measures the body of the Creator in parasangs, translated from the Hebrew of the Siddur Rabbah recension, with notes.
descriptions.verificationNote: This translation is produced from a best-effort reconstruction of the Hebrew Shi'ur Qomah text. The sense of each unit is well-attested across multiple scholarly editions (Cohen 1985, Schäfer 1981, Jellinek 1853 PD); recension-level variants between Siddur Rabbah and the other four recensions Cohen identified are documented as glossary entries where relevant. Verification of the precise textual transmission against Cohen 1985 TSAJ 9 is pending; corrections welcome.
descriptions.lensRiskNote: Shi'ur Qomah carries a distinctive lens-risk landscape compared to the rest of the WoH corpus: (a) extreme anthropomorphism of the divine, condemned by Maimonides; (b) magical-name traditions per limb (gnostic-adjacent reception); (c) cosmic-body description with surface similarity to Sitchin-Anunnaki and ancient-astronaut readings (the Raëlian canon's implicit citation of the *parasangs* makes this disavowal especially important — WoH does NOT collapse Shi'ur Qomah into the Anunnaki-deity-body framework); (d) gnostic-syncretist readings (Scholem 1965 argued for Hellenistic-gnostic influence; later scholarship — Halperin 1988, Schäfer 1992, Boustan 2005 — has nuanced or contested this). The Editor and Reviewer pipeline produces named-scholarship attributions at every claim site.
